brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Level 0 holds a full hex base (piece 0,0,0), two half bases (half-s at 0,-1 and half-n at 0,1) and a full base on level 1 (piece 0,0,1) stacked on it, so the tower is two storeys tall. All open faces are capped and joints bolted; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.

requirements.requirement: Workbench storage with at least two drawers
requirements.evidence: Two drawers were added on the cut faces of the half bases: drawer:0#0,-1#cut (key n) and drawer:0#0,1#cut (key s). Drawers were only offered once half bases were placed beside the full base.
The tower is a compact stack of hex bases with drawers on the bottom storey; I did not verify fit against a specific bench, and no bench dimensions were given. No mounting fixings were added.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex storage tower: a full base with a stacked full base above it on level 1, flanked on level 0 by two half bases carrying one drawer each (two drawers total). Open faces are capped and joints locked; the configurator check is clean with meshClash clear. Materials and load capacity of the printed parts were not assessed.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
